section_2_cross_process_event_flow.summary: 5 hops from pi child process stdout to the Pinia store. No hop adds any envelope, identifier, or version field. Events reach the renderer as the raw pi payload object only.

hops.name: pi child process stdout -> JSONL framer
hops.process: main (child stdout piped into main process)
hops.data_structure: raw UTF-8 byte chunks -> LF-delimited string lines (trailing \r tolerated, empty lines dropped: jsonl.ts:20-26)
hops.transformations: StringDecoder buffering (jsonl.ts:13-17); deliberately not Node readline to avoid U+2028/U+2029 splitting (jsonl.ts:4-8)
hops.loss_or_reorder_risk: unparseable lines are silently dropped one hop later (client.ts:118-121)

hops.name: PiRpcClient.handleLine -> EventEmitter
hops.data_structure: JSON.parse -> Record<string, unknown>, dispatched by obj.type into three lanes
dispatch_rules: type === "response" AND resp.id in pending -> resolve the awaiting Promise (client.ts:122-129)
type === "response" without matching id -> re-emitted on the "event" lane (client.ts:131)
hops.identifiers_carried: only the RPC correlation id for responses; it is generated client-side as `c${++this.seq}` (client.ts:155) and exists solely for request/response pairing. Events carry no id from this mechanism.

hops.name: main-process merge/batch forwarder
hops.data_structure: AgentEvent[] queue -> collapsed AgentEvent[] -> individual wc.send("pi:event", e) calls (ipc.ts:70)
hops.batching: 33ms setTimeout tick (ipc.ts:75); queue drained and cleared on flush (ipc.ts:69)
collapse_rules: consecutive message_update events collapse to the last one (ipc.ts:49-56) — justified because each carries the full partial message
consecutive tool_execution_update events with the same toolCallId collapse to the last one (ipc.ts:57-66)
hops.identifiers_carried: none added. Collapsing uses the event-intrinsic toolCallId only, read via an inline structural cast (ipc.ts:61-62).
hops.loss_or_reorder_risk: intermediate events are dropped by design; because no sequence number exists on the wire, the renderer has no way to detect a drop or a gap. Events queued before a client swap are still flushed to the same webContents (queue is per-forwarder closure, and a new pi:start creates a new forwarder while the old timer may still fire: ipc.ts:93-100)
hops.delivery_guard: wc.isDestroyed() check before send (ipc.ts:42) and before ui-request/exit sends (ipc.ts:101-102)

hops.name: preload contextBridge relay
hops.data_structure: ipcRenderer.on listener strips the IpcRendererEvent and passes only payload: unknown to the callback (preload/index.ts:8)
hops.identifiers_carried: none added; the sender identity available on the IpcRendererEvent is discarded
hops.transformations: structured-clone across the context bridge; returns an unsubscribe closure (preload/index.ts:10)
hops.typing: implementation is fully untyped (unknown); the AgentEvent type reappears only in the ambient declaration at packages/app/src/preload/index.d.ts:51-53

hops.name: renderer Pinia store reducer
hops.data_structure: switch on e.type mutating flat store refs; per-branch inline Extract<AgentEvent, {type: ...}> casts (stores/app.ts:183, 195, 201, 213, 224, 229)
hops.identifiers_carried: none — no session/runtime scoping. toolRuns is keyed by the event-intrinsic toolCallId only (stores/app.ts:184, 196, 202)
handled_event_types: agent_settled -> streaming=false, liveAssistant=null, then fires refreshStats/refreshSessions/refreshState (stores/app.ts:139-145)
hops.side_effect_note: activityTick is incremented for 6 event types before the switch (stores/app.ts:124-134) as a scroll trigger
hops.dedup_hack: user message_end is deduped by comparing text against the last user item in the list, because renderer optimistically inserts sent messages (stores/app.ts:163-179, insertion at stores/app.ts:417-421) — a content-equality heuristic standing in for a missing message identifier

identifier_presence.protocolVersion: absent — zero occurrences across packages/app/src and packages/pi-sdk/src
identifier_presence.workspaceId: absent — workspace is only a raw filesystem path string, passed per-call (ipc.ts:91, ipc.ts:127) and stored as AppSettings.workspace (settings.ts:6)
identifier_presence.sessionId: absent on the event wire. Exists only as a pull-model field inside AgentState.sessionId (packages/pi-sdk/src/types.ts:151) and SessionStats.sessionId (types.ts:161), plus SessionMeta.id derived from the jsonl file (sessions-store.ts:67-68). No pi:event payload carries it.
identifier_presence.runtimeId: absent — the runtime is identified only by the Electron webContents id used as the clients Map key (ipc.ts:14, 24, 93, 104), which never crosses the IPC boundary
identifier_presence.generation: absent — a pi:start after a prior start silently replaces the client (ipc.ts:93) with no generation counter, so stale in-flight events are indistinguishable from current ones
identifier_presence.sequence: absent — no monotonic counter on events. The only counter is PiRpcClient.seq (client.ts:62, 155), used for RPC request ids, never attached to events.
identifier_presence.occurredAt: absent — no emit-time timestamp. Some message payloads carry an optional producer-side timestamp?: number (types.ts:57, 69, 80, 91), and the renderer synthesizes Date.now() for locally inserted user messages (stores/app.ts:420), but no event envelope has a time field.

command_direction_flow.summary: Renderer command path is a straight pass-through with no intermediate model.
hops: renderer builds a bare object literal (stores/app.ts:402-407, 447-450, 468) — no builder/factory
main resolves client by event.sender.id then forwards verbatim (ipc.ts:115-117 -> client.ts:154-165)
PiRpcClient injects an id and writes JSON + \n to child stdin (client.ts:155, 159, 150)
response resolved by id lookup in the pending Map (client.ts:122-129), returned through the same chain
command_direction_flow.note: PiRpcClient exposes typed command wrappers (prompt/steer/followUp/abort/newSession/switchSession/setModel/... at client.ts:182-255) but the renderer bypasses all of them, sending raw literals through the generic pi:command channel. Only getState/getAvailableModels/getMessages are used via wrappers, and only inside the pi:start handler (ipc.ts:106-110).
